description: Digital oscillator carrying 47 synthesis models, from analogue waveforms and wavetables to physical models, speech and drum circuits, each shaped by two parameters

params.text: Detunes by up to a semitone either way
Sets the pitch in octaves, from five octaves below the middle C of the oscillator to three above it
Attenuverts the FM input, which shifts the pitch by one octave per volt at full clockwise; with META switched on it scales that input's control of the model instead
Sets the first shaping parameter of the model in use, which is the waveform sweep, the wavefolder amount, the sync interval or the filter cutoff depending on which model that is
Attenuverts the TIMBRE input, which adds to the TIMBRE knob
Sets the second shaping parameter of the model in use, which is the detuning, the feedback amount, the formant shift or the brightness depending on which model that is
Steps through the 47 models; the four-letter code of the one in use shows on the display

inputs.text: A rising edge past 1V strikes the physical models and resets the phase of the other models
Sets the pitch, one volt per octave, added to the two frequency knobs
Shifts the pitch, scaled and inverted by the FM knob, one octave per volt at full clockwise
Adds to the TIMBRE knob through the MODULATION attenuverter, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the COLOR knob, 5V covering the whole knob range

outputs.text: The oscillator, peaking at 5V, though loudness differs from model to model

notes: the display shows the four-letter code of the model in use, and the Model menu lists all 47 codes with a description beside each one.
the module is monophonic: on a polyphonic cable only the first channel is read, and the output carries one channel.
menu: Model — picks the synthesis model from a list giving each one's four-letter display code and a short description of it
META: FM CV selects model — hands the FM input over to choosing the model, and pitch is then set by V/OCT and the frequency knobs alone
DRFT: Pitch drift — adds the slow random detuning of an analogue oscillator
SIGN: Waveform imperfections — mixes in a waveshaped copy of the output for a dirtier tone
Low CPU (disable resampling) — runs the oscillator at the engine sample rate instead of resampling from 96kHz, which costs less processing and adds aliasing

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.3:
continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 5V.

continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 5V.
